notes: Lead type: inbound SMB, developer-first. Came from article on practical ticket summarization. Preference: quick self-serve flow (hosted API) so devs can iterate. Key asks: 1) tool-calling to create/update Zendesk tickets (create_ticket, add_tag, escalate); 2) structured JSON summaries with guaranteed fields (summary, action_items[], priority, probable_topic); 3) low friction SDKs + sample code for node/python. Latency not super aggressive — okay with 200-500ms for single-turn summary, throughput ~300 tickets/day at peak. Cost sensitive — wants to understand batching/token accounting for nightly batch summarization. Security: SOC2 mandatory, SSO (SAML) for admin console, audit logs for actions. CTO quote: "We need summaries agents can trust — high precision action items, minimal hallucinations."
description: Small support automation startup building a lightweight agent that sits between Zendesk and agents. Looking to use Redwood Hosted API for rapid POC and then scale if results hold. Early-stage, self-serve preferred; wants clear docs and a predictable cost path.
